curriculum.lesson_evidence: Exploring movement means trying many different ways to move before choosing the best ones. Choose a movement idea such as stretch, twist, shake or spin, and explore it at high, middle and low levels, in different directions, and at fast and slow times. Then choose the version that best shows your idea. Make sure there is plenty of room, no slippery socks and an adult nearby. Always move at a level that is comfortable for your body, and you can explore the same idea using only your arms or hands.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Explore the idea 'stretch' in three ways: a level, a direction and a speed. Say which one you would keep for a dance about a plant growing and why.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Stretch high, stretch sideways and stretch slowly. For a plant I would keep high and slow, because plants grow upward and gradually.' Choosing from several options and giving a reason shows exploring, not just copying.

WATCH FOR
Believing that the first movement idea is always the best. Dancers explore many ideas first, and often the third or fourth idea is the most interesting.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Pick three movement words (such as swing, curl and jump) and explore each at three levels and two speeds. Write which version you chose for each and why. Show a family member your favourite, or draw stick figures if movement is not possible.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Jo explores 'twist'. High: twist the upper body with arms overhead. Low: twist while crouching. Forward: twist and step ahead. Slow: twist as if moving through honey. Quick: twist as if shaking off water. She chooses the low slow twist because it looks like a vine growing, which is her idea for the dance.

TRY FIRST
Explore the idea 'stretch' in three ways: a level, a direction and a speed. Say which one you would keep for a dance about a plant growing and why.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Stretch high, stretch sideways and stretch slowly. For a plant I would keep high and slow, because plants grow upward and gradually.' Choosing from several options and giving a reason shows exploring, not just copying.
teach_steps.explain:
Exploring movement means trying many different ways to move before choosing the best ones. Choose a movement idea such as stretch, twist, shake or spin, and explore it at high, middle and low levels, in different directions, and at fast and slow times. Then choose the version that best shows your idea. Make sure there is plenty of room, no slippery socks and an adult nearby. Always move at a level that is comfortable for your body, and you can explore the same idea using only your arms or hands.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.

teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: Exploring movement means trying many different ways to move before choosing the best ones. Choose a movement idea such as stretch, twist, shake or spin, and explore it at high, middle and low levels, in different directions, and at fast and slow times. Then choose the version that best shows your idea. Make sure there is plenty of room, no slippery socks and an adult nearby. Always move at a level that is comfortable for your body, and you can explore the same idea using only your arms or hands. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
